BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r1.claim: The oath may refer to the afternoon itself, which has signs of divine power, or to the era of Prophethood, whose duration is likened to a day or half-day and which excels as the age of the best prophet, community, and revealed book.
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r1.anchor: ويقال اقسم بالعشى الذي هو ما بين الزوال والغروب كما سم بالضحى لما فيها جميعا من دلائل القدرة

BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r2.claim: A report says that if the Prophet's community remains upright, it has a day, and if not, half a day.
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r2.anchor: عليه السلام : إن استقامت أمتي فلها يوم وإن لم تستقم فلها نصف يوم

BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r3.claim: Another reading takes ‘asr as time itself, filled with extraordinary events, and rejects blaming time for misfortune; God swears by it as a locus of divine signs and self-disclosure through attributes and acts.
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r3.anchor: ويقال اقسم بالدهر لانطوائه على أعاجيب الأمور القارة والمارة

BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r4.claim: The Prophet says not to revile time, for God is time.
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r4.anchor: لا تسبوا الدهر فإن الله هو الدهر

BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r5.claim: The ‘asr gathers the signs sworn by elsewhere in the Qur’an, concluding the sequence of oaths about dawn, sun, moon, night, day, and duha.
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r5.anchor: فلما كان العصر جامعا لجميع الآيات التي أقسم الله بها في القرآن

BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r6.claim: The Najmiyya reading says God swears by time's complete continuity because it encompasses the Prophet's sainthood, prophethood, mission, and caliphate, citing reports about his pre-eternal prophetic status and the cosmos being created for him.
BURSEVI:v10p390#2/r6.anchor: أقسم الله بكمال دوامه الزمان واستمراره لاشتماله على ولاية النبي عليه السلام ونبوته ورسالته وخلافته

QASHANI:103:1-3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:103:1-3/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:103:1-3/r1.claim: Affliction falls first on prophets, then saints, then the best people in descending order of spiritual excellence.
QASHANI:103:1-3/r1.anchor: البلاء موكل بالأنبياء ثم الأولياء ثم الأمثل فالأمثل

QASHANI:103:1-3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:103:1-3/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:103:1-3/r2.claim: Affliction is God’s whip, by which He drives His servants toward Himself.
QASHANI:103:1-3/r2.anchor: البلاء سوط من سياط الله يسوق به عباده إليه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r1.claim: Al-ʿAṣr follows al-Takāthur’s warning against wasting life amassing wealth; people would have used life wisely if they knew they must answer for this great blessing.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r1.anchor: waste all their lives in planning

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r2.claim: This sūrah explains life’s real value and the factors that make it a path to salvation or a cause of eternal punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r2.anchor: the real value and importance of life is divulged

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r3.claim: The oath points to a lifespan as a person’s real investment: using it well earns God’s favor, while wasting it brings Hell; time can serve either the person or Satan.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r3.anchor: this time period is like a sword which can be used in both ways

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r4.claim: Only the present is available to shape; the past cannot return and the future is hidden, with its own demands.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r4.anchor: which is hidden to him and no one knows its extent

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r1.claim: A person cannot defer a present obligation to an uncertain future.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r1.anchor: defer his present obligation to the future.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p435/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p435/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p435/r1.claim: The opening particle wa means that time bears witness, and ʿaṣr means a period of time.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p435/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p435/r2.speaker: Ḥam īd al-Dīn Far āhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p435/r2.claim: Farāhī distinguishes ʿaṣr from dahr: ʿaṣr emphasizes time moving swiftly forward and is commonly used for time that has passed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p435/r2.anchor: my mentor Ḥam īd al-Dīn Far āhī has written while presenting his research

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p435/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p435/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p435/r3.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays’s verse uses ʿaṣr for a past age, asking whether those who lived then now enjoy good fortune.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p435/r3.anchor: good fortune for those who were in the time of the past.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p435/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p435/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p435/r4.claim: ʿUbayd ibn al-Abras describes an ʿaṣr when he saw himself riding a young, beautiful she-camel.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p435/r4.anchor: Fa dh āka ‘a ṣru ṇ wa qad ar ānī

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p436/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p436/r1.speaker: Im ām Far āhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p436/r1.claim: Farāhī says ʿaṣr evokes both past events and their swift passage, prompting belief in divine recompense and diligence in using time.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p436/r1.anchor: Im ām Far āhī summarizes the discussion thus:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p436/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p436/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p436/r2.claim: The oath recalls historical examples of divine reward and punishment and urges people to use fleeting moments to gain an eternal kingdom rather than a curse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p436/r2.anchor: the Almighty has directed our attention to the various events of history

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p436/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p436/r3.speaker: Im ām Far āhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p436/r3.claim: Farāhī says earlier peoples received exact recompense: virtue brought ascendancy, while oppression and disorder led to destruction after a clarifying respite; the oath warns later people of the same law.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p436/r3.anchor: Im ām Far āhī has explained this point in the following words in his exegesis:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p437/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p437/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p437/r1.claim: Time is a person’s real investment and its speed its defining feature; trusting it while ignoring worldly transience and judgment is naïve.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p437/r1.anchor: the real investment a person has is that of time

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p437/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p437/r2.speaker: Im ām Far āhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p437/r2.claim: Farāhī compares people who fail to use time to a merchant who admires melting ice instead of selling it for profit, and later regrets the loss.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p437/r2.anchor: Im ām Far āhī cites an example to explain this reality:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p437/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p437/r3.speaker: Im ām Far āhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p437/r3.claim: The speed of time also offers hope: a wise person can endure brief self-discipline to gain eternal pleasure, while one lured by worldly pleasure forfeits it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p437/r3.anchor: In this regard, Im ām Far āhī has directed our attention to another aspect:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p437/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p437/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p437/r4.claim: The lifespan is valuable yet rapidly consumed, so everyone is losing except those who believe and do good deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p437/r4.anchor: all people are in a state of loss except those who

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p394/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p394/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p394/r1.claim: Hasan says al-Asr refers to evening.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p394/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ والعصر ﴾ قال هو العشي

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p394/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p394/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p394/r2.claim: Qatada calls al-Asr one of the periods of daytime.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p394/r2.anchor: قال معمر وقال قتادة ساعة من ساعات النهار

QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r1.claim: Whoever hears God's name does not withhold wealth from it, knowing that God will make his final outcome good.
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r1.anchor: كلمة من سمعها لم يدخر عنها ماله

QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r2.claim: Whoever knows God's name does not prefer himself over it, since his intimacy was not found apart from it.
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r2.anchor: ومن عرفها لم يؤثر عليها نفسه

QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r3.claim: Whoever accompanies God's name does not withhold his spirit from it, having been granted eternal life through it.
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r3.anchor: كلمة من صحبها لم يمنع عنها روحه

QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r4.claim: Al-ʿAṣr means time or the age, by which God swears.

QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r5.claim: Another interpretation of al-ʿAṣr is the afternoon prayer.

QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r6.claim: Another interpretation of al-ʿAṣr is evening.
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r6.anchor: ويقال : أراد به صلاة العصر . ويقال : هو العشي

SULAMI:v2p419#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p419#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p419#2/r1.claim: Humanity is in loss when people neglect God's rights, follow desires, and do not fear Him.
SULAMI:v2p419#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : إذا لم يراع حقوق الله عليه ، واتبع الشهوات ولم يخش الله

TUSTARI:103:1/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:103:1/r1.speaker: قيل
TUSTARI:103:1/r1.claim: One interpretation takes the oath as invoking the Lord of Time.

TUSTARI:103:1/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:103:1/r2.speaker: قيل
TUSTARI:103:1/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes it as the afternoon or time itself.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وابن الزبير والجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn al-Zubayr, and most authorities say the surah is Meccan; Mujāhid, Qatada, and Muqātil say Madinan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية في قول ابن عباس وابن الزبير والجمهور، ومدنية في قول مجاهد وقتادة ومقاتل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r2.claim: After the previous warning against rivalry and repeated threat, this surah distinguishes the state of believer from unbeliever.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r2.anchor: لما قال فيما قبلها: ألهاكم التكاثر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says al-ʿaṣr is time, whose passing brings many remarkable events.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r3.anchor: والعصر، قال ابن عباس: هو الدهر، يقال فيه عصر وعصر وعصر أقسم به تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r4.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r4.claim: Qatada says al-ʿaṣr is late afternoon, a sign of divine power like the forenoon.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: العصر: العشي، أقسم به كما أقسم بالضحى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r5.claim: Other views take it as a day and night together, or as either the morning or evening, the two cool periods, without specifying which.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r5.anchor: وقيل: العصر: اليوم والليلة، ومنه قول حميد بن ثور:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r6.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r6.claim: Muqātil says al-ʿaṣr is the middle prayer; al-Zamakhsharī opens with this view, citing the virtue of the afternoon prayer and the report that missing it is like losing family and wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل: العصر: الصلاة الوسطى، أقسم بها. وبهذا القول بدأ الزمخشري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains that the afternoon prayer is hard to maintain when people are busy with trade and end-of-day accounts; Salam also reads al-ʿaṣr and al-ṣabr with kasra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r7.anchor: لأن التنكيف في أدائها أشق لتهافت الناس في تجاراتهم وتحاسبهم آخر النهار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the kasra readings occur only at pause through transferred vowel; Abu ʿAmr reports and other grammarians describe related pause or movement readings, supported by poetic examples.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r8.anchor: وقرأ سلام: والعصر بكسر الصاد، والصبر بكسر الباء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r1.speaker: الراجز
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r1.claim: A rajaz verse ending with fī al-ʿaṣr is cited to show the transferred vowel as evidence for the reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r1.anchor: أنا جرير كنيتي أبو عمر ... أضرب بالسيف وسعد في العصر

FARRA:v3p289/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p289/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p289/r1.claim: Al-ʿaṣr means time or the age; God swears by it.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p538#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p538#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p538#6/r1.claim: Al-ʿaṣr means time or the age, by which God swears.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r1.claim: Muqatil says the oath is by the Asr prayer because of its virtue; the majority identify it as the middle prayer, supported by reports naming it and warning against missing it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل أقسم سبحانه بصلاة العصر لفضلها لانها الصلاة الوسطى عند الجمهور

ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r2.claim: The author dismisses a story about a sinful woman being told her gravest sin was missing Asr prayer as unreliable material from an otherwise prominent transmitter.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r2.anchor: ذكر ذلك الامام وهو لعمري امام في نقل مثل ذلك مما لايعول عليه عند أئمة الحديث

ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r3.claim: Asr prayer is especially meritorious because people neglect it while absorbed in trade and work late in the day.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r3.anchor: وخصت بالفضل لان التكليف في أدائها أشق لتهافت الناس في تجاراتهم ومكاسبهم آخر النهار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r4.claim: Qatada says the oath is by the time of the Asr prayer, or by the creation of Adam on Friday; he also explains al-asr as evening, rich in signs of divine power like dawn.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r4.anchor: وقيل أقسم عز وجل بوقت تلك الصلاة لفضيلة صلاته أو لخلق آدم أبي البشر عليه السلام فيه من يوم الجمعة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says al-asr means day or night, and cites Hamid ibn Thawr's verse about the two spans of time, day and night.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r5.anchor: وقال الزجاج العصر اليوم والعصر الليلة وعليه قول حميد بن ثور

ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r6.claim: Some interpret al-asr as morning and evening, the two cool periods; on this and the preceding view the oath is to one of two unspecified times.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r6.anchor: وقيل العصر بكرة والعصر عشية وهما الابرادان

ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r7.claim: Some take al-asr as the Prophet's era or his lifetime through the Resurrection, whose remaining span is compared in a Bukhari report to the time from Asr to sunset; its honor comes from the Prophet and his community.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد به عصر النبوة وكأنه عنى به وقت حياته عليه الصلاة والسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-asr is time itself, encompassing wonders and blessings as well as their opposites; the oath warns people facing ruin or salvation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس هو الدهر أقسم عز وجل به لاشتماله على أصناف العجائب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r9.claim: The oath honors time while denying that time itself causes loss or events, as some claim; attributing loss to humanity shows it is a human quality, not a defect of time.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227#2/r9.anchor: ويعرض عز وجل لما في الاقسام به من التعظيم بنفي أن يكون له خسران أو دخل فيه كما يزعمه من يضيف الحوادث اليه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p228/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228/r1.claim: The author objects that using al-asr to mean time in general is not linguistically apparent.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228/r1.anchor: وتعقب بان استعمال العصر بذلك المعنى غير ظاهر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets al-asr as time or the ages.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r2.claim: One explanation says time is sworn by because it offers lessons to anyone who reflects.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r2.anchor: قيل: أقسم به لأن فيه عبرة للناظر.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r3.claim: Another explanation takes the oath to mean “by the Lord of time,” as in comparable oaths.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: معناه ورب العصر، وكذلك في أمثاله.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r4.speaker: ابن كيسان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kaysan says al-asr means both night and day, which are called the two asrs.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r4.anchor: واقل ابن كيسان: أراد بالعصر الليل والنهار، يقال لهما العصران.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r5.claim: Hasan identifies al-asr as the time from noon's decline until sunset.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن: من بعد زوال الشمس إلى غروبها (2) .

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r6.claim: Qatada identifies it as the final hour of the day.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: آخر ساعة من ساعات النهار (3) .

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r7.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r7.claim: Maqatil interprets the oath as the afternoon prayer, which is the middle prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r7.anchor: وقال مقاتل: أقسم بصلاة العصر وهي الصلاة الوسطى.

BAYDAWI-FULL:103:1-3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:103:1-3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:103:1-3/r1.claim: العصر may mean the afternoon prayer for its merit, the prophetic era, or time itself, whose marvels also counter claims that time causes misfortune.
BAYDAWI-FULL:103:1-3/r1.anchor: { والعصر } أقسم سبحانه بصلاة العصر لفضلها، أو بعصر النبوة أو بالدهر

BINTSHATI:v2p75/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p75/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p75/r2.claim: The root sense of asr is pressing to extract juice, as in squeezing grapes; related words name the press, place of pressing, and stones used for it.
BINTSHATI:v2p75/r2.anchor: والمعنى الأصلي للعصر لغة: الضغط لاستخلاص العصارة

BINTSHATI:v2p75/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p75/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p75/r3.claim: Arabic also calls rain-bearing clouds mu'sirat, says a people asaru when they bring rain, and uses i'sar for a strong wind driving clouds.
BINTSHATI:v2p75/r3.anchor: وسميت السحب الممطرة معصرات لما تعتصر من المطر، وأعصر القوم أمطروا

BINTSHATI:v2p75/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p75/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p75/r4.claim: Arabic also uses asr metaphorically for confinement and extraction by pressure, and derives words for age and lineage from the image of pressing out an essence.
BINTSHATI:v2p75/r4.anchor: ومن هذه الدلالة اللغوية الأصلية على الضغط والإعتصار

BINTSHATI:v2p75/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p75/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p75/r5.claim: The age is called asr because experience and hardship press out a person's essence; late afternoon is also asr as the day is brought to its close, and the prayer takes its name from that time.
BINTSHATI:v2p75/r5.anchor: سمي الدهر عصراً، بملحظ من استخلاصه عصارة الإنسان بالضغط والتجربة

BINTSHATI:v2p75/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p75/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p75/r6.claim: Quranic uses of the root include squeezing grapes in Yusuf 12:36 and rain clouds in al-Naba 78:14, alongside the verb in Yusuf 12:49.
BINTSHATI:v2p75/r6.anchor: بمعناه اللغوي الأول في اعتصار الخمر بآية يوسف 36

BINTSHATI:v2p76/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p76/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p76/r1.claim: The root also appears for a whirlwind in al-Baqara 2:266 and for asr in the surah itself.
BINTSHATI:v2p76/r1.anchor: والإعصار في آية البقرة 266. والعصر، في سورة العصر

BINTSHATI:v2p76/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p76/r2.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI:v2p76/r2.claim: Among the meanings of the oath, al-Tabari reports both the age and a particular time of day, then prefers the age.

BINTSHATI:v2p76/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p76/r3.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p76/r3.claim: Al-Razi lists the afternoon prayer, understood with an omitted noun, and the age of Prophethood among the proposed meanings, without an explicit preference.
BINTSHATI:v2p76/r3.anchor: وقيل أنه صلاة العصر، على حذف المضاف، أو هو عصر النبوة

BINTSHATI:v2p76/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p76/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v2p76/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari appears to prefer the afternoon prayer because of its merit and difficulty during the busy end of the workday; he cites the report comparing a missed prayer to losing one's family and property.
BINTSHATI:v2p76/r4.anchor: ولأن التكليف في أدائها أشق لتهافت الناس في تجارتهم ومكاسبهم آخر النهار

BINTSHATI:v2p76/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p76/r5.speaker: محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v2p76/r5.claim: Muhammad Abdu says Arabs gathered at afternoon to talk, so the oath corrects the belief that time itself is blameworthy when harmful conduct may occur then.
BINTSHATI:v2p76/r5.anchor: وكان من عادة العرب أن يجتمعوا وقت العصر، ويتحادثوا ويتذكروا

BINTSHATI:v2p76/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p76/r6.speaker: ابن قيم الجوزية
BINTSHATI:v2p76/r6.claim: Ibn Qayyim prefers reading asr as the age, as do most exegetes.
BINTSHATI:v2p76/r6.anchor: الراجح عند "ابن قيم الجوزية" أنه الدهر

BINTSHATI:v2p77/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p77/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p77/r1.claim: The oath's waw retains its basic linguistic force of magnifying what is sworn by; al-Tabari did not construct elaborate arguments for the greatness of asr.
BINTSHATI:v2p77/r1.anchor: والسورة تبدأ بواو القسم وهو عندهم على أصل استعماله اللغوي

BINTSHATI:v2p77/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p77/r2.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p77/r2.claim: Al-Razi assembles six reasons for the greatness of the age, three for a particular time of day, six for the afternoon prayer, and a further case for the Prophetic age.
BINTSHATI:v2p77/r2.anchor: جمع الرازي ستة وجوه في عظمة العصر بمعنى الدهر

BINTSHATI:v2p77/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p77/r3.speaker: محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v2p77/r3.claim: The author rejects Muhammad Abdu's claim that afternoon was the customary time for gatherings: evening may fit better, and objectionable talk is possible at any time.
BINTSHATI:v2p77/r3.anchor: ولا نعلم أن هذا الوقت في المألوف والعادة وقت اجتماع الناس وتذاكرهم

BINTSHATI:v2p77/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p77/r4.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p77/r4.claim: Al-Razi's reasons for magnifying the age include its extraordinary changes, the value of the final moment of life, and time's rank over space.
BINTSHATI:v2p77/r4.anchor: ولا تكاد أقوالهم تخرج عما استوفاه الفخر الرازي من وجوه عظمة العصر

BINTSHATI:v2p77/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p77/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p77/r5.claim: The author follows al-Tabari, Ibn Qayyim, and most exegetes in reading asr as the age, and confines discussion to the arguments offered for that meaning.
BINTSHATI:v2p77/r5.anchor: ومن حيث آثرنا مع الطبري وابن القيم، وأكثر المفسرين، أن يكون العصر بمعنى الدهر

BINTSHATI:v2p78/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p78/r1.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p78/r1.claim: Al-Razi calls time a wonder encompassing fortune and hardship, health and illness, and wealth and poverty, while resisting simple judgments that it either exists or does not.
BINTSHATI:v2p78/r1.anchor: فعلمت حينئذ أن أشرف الأشياء حياتك في هذه اللمحة

BINTSHATI:v2p78/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p78/r2.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p78/r2.claim: Al-Razi says even a final instant can secure eternal paradise after a wasted lifetime, making time one of the greatest blessings.
BINTSHATI:v2p78/r2.anchor: إن بقية عمر المرء لا قيمة لها، فلو ضيعت ألف سنة

BINTSHATI:v2p78/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p78/r3.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p78/r3.claim: Al-Razi regards time as nobler than space and says the oath answers people who blame the age for calamities: the fault lies in the human being, not time.
BINTSHATI:v2p78/r3.anchor: إن الزمان أعلى وأشرف من المكان، فكان القسم بالعصر قسماً بأشرف النصفين

BINTSHATI:v2p78/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p78/r5.speaker: ابن القيم
BINTSHATI:v2p78/r5.claim: Ibn Qayyim sees the ordered alternation of night and day, their changing light and temperature, and time divisions as signs of God's power and wisdom; the oath links human actions in time to their judgment.
BINTSHATI:v2p78/r5.anchor: فأقسم بالعصر الذي هو زمان أفعال الإنسان ومحلها، على عاقبة تلك الأفعال وجزائها

BINTSHATI:v2p78/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p78/r6.speaker: النيسابوري
BINTSHATI:v2p78/r6.claim: Al-Nisaburi compares evening to the world's destruction and morning to resurrection, urging people to use their remaining lifespan for a trade without loss.
BINTSHATI:v2p78/r6.anchor: أن آخر النهار يشبه تخريب العالم وإماتة الأحياء كما أن أول النهار يشبه بعث الأموات

BINTSHATI:v2p79/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p79/r1.speaker: النيسابوري
BINTSHATI:v2p79/r1.claim: Al-Nisaburi says the world's remaining life is like the time between afternoon and sunset, so people should hasten a trade without loss.
BINTSHATI:v2p79/r1.anchor: الدنيا ما بقى إلا بقدر ما بين العصر إلى المغرب، فعلى الإنسان أن يشتغل بتجارة لا خسران فيها

BINTSHATI:v2p79/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p79/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p79/r2.claim: The author cites the prophetic report against blaming time, since God is al-dahr.
BINTSHATI:v2p79/r2.anchor: ولذلك قال - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: لا تسبوا الدهر فإن الله هو الدهر

BINTSHATI:v2p79/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p79/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p79/r3.claim: A report describes time as strangely both existent and like nothing, and compares a person's lifetime to a small part of it.
BINTSHATI:v2p79/r3.anchor: من أعجايب الدهر الدالة على كمال قدره خالقها: أن الدهر موجود يشبه المعدوم

BINTSHATI:v2p79/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p79/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p79/r4.claim: The author rejects loading asr with philosophical and mystical interpretations; the Quran explains signs of night and day in accessible terms, as in al-Qasas 28:71-72.
BINTSHATI:v2p79/r4.anchor: وترى أنهم حملوا لفظ العصر كل هذه التأويلات الفلسفية والإشارية مما

BINTSHATI:v2p80/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p80/r1.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p80/r1.claim: Al-Razi suggests the Quran chose asr instead of dahr because unbelievers were fond of invoking and exalting the latter word.
BINTSHATI:v2p80/r1.anchor: ولعله تعالى لم يذكر الدهر لعلمه أن الملحد مولع بذكره وتعظيمه

BINTSHATI:v2p80/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p80/r2.speaker: النيسابوري
BINTSHATI:v2p80/r2.claim: Al-Nisaburi explains the oath as honoring the age and cites the report that people should not curse time because God is al-dahr.
BINTSHATI:v2p80/r2.anchor: على حين يذهب النيسابورى إلى أن وجه الإقسام بالعصر هنا

BINTSHATI:v2p80/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p80/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p80/r4.claim: The oath's waw moves from a perceptible reality to a moral truth, a pattern the author also discusses in other surahs.
BINTSHATI:v2p80/r4.anchor: الواو هنا في موضعها الذي تطرد به الظاهرة الأسلوبية في اللفت إلى حسى مدرك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r1.speaker: الشافعي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r1.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says this surah would suffice people if no other revelation had come; another reported view says it gathers all Qur'anic sciences.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r1.anchor: قال الإمام الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه : إنها سورة لو لم ينزل إلى الناس إلا هي لكفتهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r2.claim: The surah distinguishes the saved human essence from the doomed and teaches salvation by leaving the transient for the lasting; the name al-ʿAṣr signals extraction of an essence.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r2.anchor: مقصودها تفضيل نوع الإنسان المخلوق من علق ، وبيان خلاصته وعصارته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r3.claim: The author associates the name with the Prophet's era and the afternoon prayer, which he calls the best of the prayers.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r3.anchor: ولذلك كان وقت هذا النبي الخاتم الذي هو خلاصة الخلق وقت العصر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r4.speaker: الغزالي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r4.claim: Al-Ghazālī likens the Qur'an to a sea containing six minerals: knowledge of God, His attributes and acts, the afterlife, worship, doubts that harm faith, and lessons from the saved and ruined.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r4.anchor: على ما قال الغزالي : إن القرآن كالبحر الذي فيه جزائر بها معادن ستة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r5.claim: The surah begins with examples of the ruined and saved because preventing harm precedes securing benefit.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r5.anchor: وبدئ بها لأن درء المفاسد مقدم على جلب المصالح

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r6.claim: The surah's other clauses map to knowledge of God and the afterlife, required and preparatory worship, and patience that completes the effort to avoid doubt and harm.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r6.anchor: والخامسة وسيلة إليها ومتمة لها لأن معرفة ذلك واجتنابه لا يكون إلا ببذل الجهد في الصبر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r7.claim: The basmala says all things perish except God, whose mercy reaches everyone and whose completed gifts distinguish His chosen allies.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r7.anchor: بسم الله } الذي كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه { الرحمن

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r1.speaker: الشافعي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r1.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says this surah would suffice people if no other revelation had come; another reported view says it gathers all Qur'anic sciences.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r1.anchor: قال الإمام الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه : إنها سورة لو لم ينزل إلى الناس إلا هي لكفتهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r2.claim: The surah distinguishes the saved human essence from the doomed and teaches salvation by leaving the transient for the lasting; the name al-ʿAṣr signals extraction of an essence.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r2.anchor: مقصودها تفضيل نوع الإنسان المخلوق من علق ، وبيان خلاصته وعصارته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r3.claim: The author associates the name with the Prophet's era and the afternoon prayer, which he calls the best of the prayers.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r3.anchor: ولذلك كان وقت هذا النبي الخاتم الذي هو خلاصة الخلق وقت العصر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r4.speaker: الغزالي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r4.claim: Al-Ghazālī likens the Qur'an to a sea containing six minerals: knowledge of God, His attributes and acts, the afterlife, worship, doubts that harm faith, and lessons from the saved and ruined.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r4.anchor: على ما قال الغزالي : إن القرآن كالبحر الذي فيه جزائر بها معادن ستة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r5.claim: The surah begins with examples of the ruined and saved because preventing harm precedes securing benefit.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r5.anchor: وبدئ بها لأن درء المفاسد مقدم على جلب المصالح

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r6.claim: The surah's other clauses map to knowledge of God and the afterlife, required and preparatory worship, and patience that completes the effort to avoid doubt and harm.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r6.anchor: والخامسة وسيلة إليها ومتمة لها لأن معرفة ذلك واجتنابه لا يكون إلا ببذل الجهد في الصبر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r7.claim: The basmala says all things perish except God, whose mercy reaches everyone and whose completed gifts distinguish His chosen allies.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r7.anchor: بسم الله } الذي كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه { الرحمن

BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r1.claim: The surah continues al-Takāthur's warning about worldly pleasures and the threat of Hell: people in this life face grave danger and their pleasures are clouded.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r1.anchor: ختم التكاثر عن ذلك النعيم متوعدا برؤية الجحيم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r2.claim: Al-ʿAṣr may mean the time when Adam was created, on Friday afternoon according to a sound report in Muslim; the middle prayer or its time; the Prophet's era; each person's lifetime; the late afternoon; or all time.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r2.anchor: أي الزمان الذي خلق فيه أصله آدم عليه الصلاة والسلام وهو في عصر يوم الجمعة كما ورد في الحديث الصحيح في مسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r3.claim: The afternoon is valuable because work ends, rest begins, daily gains are gathered, and the day's remaining hours reveal who used their time profitably; the word can also evoke resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r3.anchor: أو وقت الأصيل لأنه أفضله بما يحويه من الفراغ من الأشغال واستقبال الراحة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r4.claim: The oath can encompass all time, in which God created the world and decreed events; its wonders direct people to God’s majesty and should focus their effort on Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p522/r4.anchor: أو جميع الدهر الذي أوجد فيه سبحانه وتعالى المخلوقات وقدر فيه المقدورات بما ظهر فيه من العجائب

NAHHAS:v5p286/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p286/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p286/r1.claim: The implied oath is ‘by time’; because there is no proof restricting it, ʿaṣr includes all its senses: time, late afternoon, and refuge.
NAHHAS:v5p286/r1.anchor: التقدير ورب العصر ويدخل فيه كل ما يسمى بالعصر لأنه لم يقع اختصاص تقوم به حجة فالعصر الدهر والعصر العشي والعصر الملجأ

DURR-FULL:v8p621/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p621/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p621/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Surat al-Asr was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v8p621/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت سورة {والعصر} بمكة

DURR-FULL:v8p621/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p621/r4.speaker: ميمون
DURR-FULL:v8p621/r4.claim: At Umar’s stabbing, Abd al-Rahman led Fajr and recited al-Asr; the report names al-Nasr as the other short surah.
DURR-FULL:v8p621/r4.anchor: عن ميمون قال: شهدت عمر حين طعن فأمنا عبد الرحمن بن عوف فقرأ بأقصر سورتين في القرآن بالعصر

DURR-FULL:v8p621/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p621/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p621/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-asr is an hour of the daytime.
DURR-FULL:v8p621/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس {والعصر} قال: ساعة من ساعات النهار

DURR-FULL:v8p621/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p621/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p621/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas also identifies al-asr as the late afternoon before sunset.
DURR-FULL:v8p621/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس {والعصر} قال: هو ما قبل مغيب الشمس من العشي

DURR-FULL:v8p621/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p621/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p621/r11.claim: Qatada interprets al-asr as an hour of the daytime.
DURR-FULL:v8p621/r11.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {والعصر} قال: ساعة من ساعات النهار

DURR-FULL:v8p622/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p622/r1.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
DURR-FULL:v8p622/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says God swears by the afternoon.
DURR-FULL:v8p622/r1.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي {والعصر} قال: قسم أقسم به ربنا وتبارك وتعالى

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3462/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3462/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3462/r1.claim: Qatadah identifies al-Asr as one of the hours of the day.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3462/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : والعصر قال : ساعة من ساعات النهار

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3462/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3462/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3462/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says all people are in loss; belief alone is not enough, and the verse successively requires good works, mutual counsel in truth, and mutual counsel in patience.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3462/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي والعصر قال : قسم اقسم الله به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets al-asr as time or an era, with variant vowel forms illustrated by Imru al-Qays.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: العصر: الدهر، يقال فيه عصر وعصر بضم العين والصاد،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r2.claim: Qatada says al-asr means late afternoon.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r3.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb asked the Prophet, who said God swears by the end of the day.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبي بن كعب: سألت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن العصر فقال: «أقسم ربكم بآخر النهار» ،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r4.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r4.claim: A view cited by Abu Ali says asr means day, while ʿasr means evening; a poem uses the dual for day and night.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء: وذكره أبو علي العصر: اليوم، والعصر: الليلة ومنه قول حميد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r5.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r5.claim: Some scholars identify al-asrayn with morning and evening, the two cooler parts of the day.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء: العصر: بكرة والعصر: عشية وهما الأبردان،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r6.speaker: مقاتل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r6.claim: Muqatil identifies al-asr with the middle prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#2/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل: العصر هي الصلاة الوسطى أقسم بها،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#3/r3.speaker: سلام أبو المنذر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#3/r3.claim: Salam Abu al-Mundhir reads al-asr with kasra on ṣad and al-sabr with kasra on ba, permissible only at pause through transferred vowel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ سلام أبو المنذر: «والعصر» بكسر الصاد «وبالصبر» بكسر الباء،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r2.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r2.claim: A report says that before accepting Islam, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ told Musaylima that a brief, eloquent sūra had been revealed and recited al-ʿAṣr; Musaylima answered with a parody.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r2.anchor: ذكروا أن عمرو بن العاص وفد على مسيلمة الكذاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r3.claim: Al-Wabr is a small animal resembling a cat, notable for its ears; Musaylima's incoherent imitation failed to impress even an idol-worshipper.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r3.anchor: والوبر: دويبة تشبه الهر، أعظم شيء فيه أذناه، وصدره وباقيه دميم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r4.claim: Al-Kharāʾiṭī also recorded this story, or something close to it, in the second part of his book on bad character.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r4.anchor: وقد رأيت أبا بكر الخرائطي أسند (4) في كتابه المعروف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن حصن أبو مدينة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī reports that two Companions would recite Sūrat al-ʿAṣr to each other whenever they met, then exchange greetings before parting.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن حصن [أبي مدينة] ، قال: كان الرجلان من أصحاب رسول الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r6.speaker: الشافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r6.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says that if people reflected on this sūra, it would suffice them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r6.anchor: وقال الشافعي، رحمه الله: لو تدبر الناس هذه السورة، لوسعتهم

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r1.speaker: أبي
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet promises that reciting Sūrat al-ʿAṣr brings patience and companionship with the people of truth on the Resurrection Day.
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r1.anchor: وعن أبي عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ سورة (والعصر) ختم الله له بالصبر

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r2.claim: After warning about those distracted by worldly abundance, this chapter says people are in loss unless they do good and avoid disobedience.
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r2.anchor: ولما ختم السورة بوعيد من ألهاه التكاثر بالدنيا، افتتح هذه السورة بأن الإنسان في خسر

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r4.claim: Al-ʿaṣr means time, from wringing moisture out of cloth; the image is extended to time as the span in which affairs are worked and turned.
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r4.anchor: العصر: الدهر، وأصله: عصر الثوب ونحوه، وهو فتله لإخراج مائه

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r5.claim: The afternoon prayer is named for being deferred from the beginning of its time; ʿaṣāra is what is pressed from grapes, while muʿṣirāt are rain-bearing clouds.
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r5.anchor: ومنه سميت صلاة العصر؛ لأنها تعصر بالتأخير عن أول وقتها

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r6.claim: Iʿṣār is a column of dust that twists and rises into the sky.
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r6.anchor: والإعصار: غبار ينفتل كالعمود، ويتصعد في السماء

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r9.claim: The wāw in al-ʿaṣr is an oath particle; the oath's answer is “humanity is surely in loss.”
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r9.anchor: والعصر) مكسور لأنه قسم، والواو واو القسم، وموضع القسم قوله: (إن الإنسان لفي خسر)

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r13.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r13.claim: They identify al-ʿaṣr as the age or time, whose passing days and changing conditions provide a lesson.
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r13.anchor: والعصر: الدهر، عن ابن عباس، والكلبي، وأبي علي

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r14.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r14.claim: They identify al-ʿaṣr as late afternoon, which provides a lesson through the night approaching and day receding.
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r14.anchor: وقيل: هو العشي، عن الحسن، وقتادة

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r15.speaker: ابن كيسان
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r15.claim: He identifies al-ʿaṣr as night and day.
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r15.anchor: وقيل: الليل والنهار، عن ابن كيسان

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r16.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r16.claim: He identifies al-ʿaṣr as the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer.
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r16.anchor: وقيل: صلاة العصر، وهي الوسطى، عن مقاتل

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r17.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r17.claim: He identifies al-ʿaṣr as one end of the day.
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r17.anchor: وقيل: العصر أحد طرفي النهار، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r18.speaker: علي
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r18.claim: He identifies al-ʿaṣr as the misfortunes of time; the author prefers the first interpretation, time itself.
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r18.anchor: وقيل: العصر نوائب الدهر، عن علي. والأول الوجه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r1.claim: One interpretation is that the oath refers to the Asr prayer because of its virtue; Hafsa's codex identifies the middle prayer as Asr.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r1.anchor: أقسم بصلاة العصر لفضلها ، بدليل قوله تعالى : ( والصلاة الوسطى ) صلاة العصر ، في مصحف حفصة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r2.speaker: رسول الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r2.claim: The Prophet compares missing the Asr prayer to losing one's family and property.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r2.anchor: وقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( 1340 ) ( من فاتته العصر فكأنما وتر أهله وماله )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r3.claim: The Asr prayer is especially difficult to perform because people are absorbed in trade and livelihood late in the day.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r3.anchor: ولأن التكليف في أدائها أشق لتهافت الناس في تجاراتهم ومكاسبهم آخر النهار ، واشتغالهم بمعايشهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that the oath refers to evening, as the Qur'an also swears by forenoon; both times display signs of divine power.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r4.anchor: أو أقسم بالعشي كما أقسم بالضحى لما فيهما جميعا من دلائل القدرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r5.claim: A further interpretation is that the oath refers to time, whose passage contains many kinds of wonders.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r5.anchor: أو أقسم بالزمان لما في مروره من أصناف العجائب

SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r1.claim: The common reading has ṣād still; Salam ibn Sulaymān reads ‘al-‘aṣri’ and ‘al-ṣabri’ with kasra. Ibn ‘Atiyya allows this only at pause through vowel transfer, while an Abu ‘Amr report uses an imala-like kasra on the bā’.
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r1.anchor: وسلام " والعصر " والصبر " بكسر الصاد والباء. قال ابن عطية: ولا يجوز إلا في الوقف

SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r2.speaker: الهذلي
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r2.claim: Al-Hudhali reports the kasra reading of ‘al-‘aṣr’, ‘al-ṣabr’, ‘al-fajr’, and ‘al-watr’ from Harun and Ibn Musa on Abu ‘Amr in both pause and connected recitation.
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r2.anchor: قال الهذلي: " والعصر والصبر، والفجر، والوتر، بكسر ما قبل الساكن في هذه كلها

SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r3.speaker: ابن خالويه
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r3.claim: Ibn Khalawayh also describes Abu ‘Amr’s ‘al-ṣabri’ as vowel transfer without limiting the report to pause.
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r3.anchor: وقال ابن خالويه: " والصبر " بنقل الحركة عن أبي عمرو " فأطلق ايضا

SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r4.speaker: أبو الفضل
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r4.claim: Abu al-Fadl describes transferring the final rā’s vowel to bā’ before a pause as widespread Arabic, marking inflection, avoiding two adjacent vowelless letters, and preserving pause-sukūn.
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r4.anchor: بنقل حركة الراء إلى الباء يحتاج إلى أن يأتي ببعض الحركة في الوقف

SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r5.speaker: الشاعر
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r5.claim: The anonymous poetic examples ‘wa-ṣṭifāqan bi-r-rajul’ and ‘ana Jarir … wa-Sa‘d fi al-qaṣr’ witness transferring a vowel before a consonant cluster.
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r5.anchor: بالرجل يريد بالرجل. وقال آخر: 4637 أنا جرير كنيتي أبو عمر

SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r6.claim: Vowel transfer also occurs with ḍamma, as in the cited ‘idh jadda al-naqru’.
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r6.anchor: والنقل جائز في الضمة أيضا كقوله: 4638............. إذ جد النقر

SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r7.claim: ‘Al-‘aṣr’ can mean both night and day; a poem calls them the two ‘aṣrs’ and glosses them as a day and a night.
SAMIN-DURR:103:1/r7.anchor: والعصر: الليلة واليوم قال: 4639 ولن يلبث العصران يوم وليلة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333/r1.claim: Mawardi says the sura is Makkan, though one narration from Ibn Abbas and Qatada calls it Medinan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333/r1.anchor: مكية ، وفي إحدى الروايتين عن ابن عباس وقتادة أنها مدنية .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، زيد بن أسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and Zayd ibn Aslam say العصر is time or the passage of time.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أن العصر الدهر , قاله ابن عباس وزيد بن أسلم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r2.speaker: الحسن، قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say it is late afternoon, from the sun's decline to sunset, supported by a line of poetry.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنه العشي ما بين زوال الشمس وغروبها , قاله الحسن وقتادة , ومنه قول الشاعر :

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r3.claim: Mawardi allows that the oath refers to the Prophet's era, distinguished by renewed prophethood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r3.anchor: أن يريد عصر الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم لفضله بتجديد النبوة فيه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r4.claim: Muqatil says the oath refers to the afternoon prayer, the middle prayer and the best prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r4.anchor: وفيه رابع : أنه أراد صلاة العصر , وهي الصلاة الوسطى , لأنها أفضل الصلوات , قاله مقاتل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r5.claim: The time is singled out in the oath because it contains the closing acts of the day.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r5.anchor: وخصه بالقسم لأن فيه خواتيم الأعمال

MUQATIL:103:1-3/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r1.claim: Muqatil explains al-ʿaṣr as the late part of the day, its last hour.
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r1.anchor: أقسم الله عز وجل بعصر النهار، وهو آخر ساعة من النهار

MUQATIL:103:1-3/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r2.claim: As the sun declines toward sunset, God also swears by the ʿAṣr prayer.
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r2.anchor: وأيضا العصر سميت العصر حين تصوبت الشمس للغروب، وهو عصر النهار، فأقسم الله عز وجل بصلاة العصر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p355#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p355#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p355#6/r1.claim: The oath may be by the afternoon prayer, whose merit is shown by Hafsa's codex identifying it as the middle prayer; performing it is difficult amid late-day trade and work.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p355#6/r1.anchor: أقسم بصلاة العصر لفضلها بدليل قوله تعالى والصلاة الوسطى صلاة العصر فى مصحف حفصة ولأن التكليف فى أدائها شق

NASAFI-FULL:v4p355#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p355#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p355#6/r2.claim: Alternatively, the oath is by evening, as the surah swears by duha, because evening displays God's power.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p355#6/r2.anchor: أو أقسم بالعشى كما أقسم بالضحى لما فيها من دلائل القدرة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p355#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p355#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p355#6/r3.claim: Alternatively, the oath is by time, whose passage contains many kinds of wonders.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p355#6/r3.anchor: أو أقسم بالزمان لما فى مروره من أصناف العجائب

QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and others say al-asr means time or age; its changing conditions point to the Creator.
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r1.anchor: أي الدهر قاله ابن عباس وغيره. فالعصر مثل الدهر

QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r2.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r2.claim: A poem uses the contrast of a day, month, and age to illustrate time's scale.
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r2.anchor: ويوم الهوى شهر وشهر الهوى دهر

QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r3.speaker: حميد بن ثور
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r3.claim: Humayd ibn Thawr uses al-asran for day and night.

QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r4.claim: Al-asran can also mean morning and evening, as in a poet's promise to repay at day's end what was asked in its morning.

QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r5.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r5.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say al-asr is the afternoon interval from the sun's decline until sunset.
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r5.anchor: وقيل: إنه العشي، وهو ما بين زوال الشمس وغروبها قاله الحسن وقتادة.

QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r6.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r6.claim: Qatada also defines al-asr as the final hour of the daytime.
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r6.anchor: وعن قتادة أيضا: هو آخر ساعة من ساعات النهار.

QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r7.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r7.claim: Muqatil says the oath invokes the afternoon prayer, the middle prayer because it is the most excellent prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو قسم بصلاة العصر، وهي الوسطى لأنها أفضل الصلوات قاله مقاتل.

QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r8.claim: An authentic report identifies the middle prayer as the Asr prayer; Qurtubi says its explanation appeared under al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r8.anchor: وفي الخبر الصحيح: " الصلاة الوسطى: صلاة العصر "

QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r9.claim: Another interpretation takes the oath as invoking the Prophet's era, honored by the renewal of prophethood in it.
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r9.anchor: وقيل: هو قسم بعصر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، لفضله بتجديد النبوة فيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r10.claim: The oath may also have an omitted object, meaning by the Lord of the age.

QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r11.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r11.claim: Malik says a person who swears not to speak to someone for an asr has sworn off speech for a year, the most expansive interpretation and consistent with his stricter approach to oaths.
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r11.anchor: قال مالك: من حلف ألا يكلم رجلا عصرا: لم يكلمه سنة.

QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r12.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r12.claim: Al-Shafi'i says the oath is fulfilled by refraining for an hour, unless the speaker intended another duration.
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r12.anchor: وقال الشافعي: يبر بساعة، إلا أن تكون له نية،

QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r13.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r13.claim: Ibn al-Arabi prefers al-Shafi'i's hour unless the person swearing is Arab, in which case the stated intended meaning is accepted if plausible, except the shortest reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:103:1/r13.anchor: وقال الشافعي: يبر بساعة، إلا أن تكون له نية، وبه أقول إلا أن يكون الحالف عربيا

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan, has three verses, and compresses Islam's full way of life and the Muslim community's identity and role into a brief constitution.

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r2.claim: The surah presents the Muslim community's essence and function in its final verse, a concise form of inimitable divine expression.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r2.anchor: وتصف الأمة المسلمة : حقيقتها ووظيفتها . في آية واحدة هي الآية الثالثة من السورة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r3.claim: Across all ages there is one successful path: faith, righteous action, and mutual exhortation to truth and patience; every other way ends in loss.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r3.anchor: ليس هنالك إلا منهج واحد رابح ، وطريق واحد ناج . هو ذلك المنهج الذي ترسم السورة حدوده

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r46.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r46.speaker: الرجلان من أصحاب رسول الله
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r46.claim: Qutb reports that two Companions would not part after meeting until one recited Surat al-Asr to the other, renewing their commitment to its guidance.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r46.anchor: كان الرجلان من أصحاب رسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] إذا التقيا لم يتفرقا حتى يقرأ أحدهما على الآخر سورة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r1.claim: Qutb treats mutual exhortation to truth and patience as defining the Muslim community's distinct identity and bond.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r1.anchor: أما التواصي بالحق والتواصي بالصبر فتبرز من خلالها صورة الأمة المسلمة - أو الجماعة المسلمة - ذات الكيان الخاص

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r2.claim: Across all ages there is one successful path: faith, righteous action, and mutual exhortation to truth and patience; every other way ends in loss.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r2.anchor: طريق واحد لا يتعدد . طريق الإيمان والعمل الصالح وقيام الجماعة المسلمة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r45.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r45.speaker: الرجلان من أصحاب رسول الله
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r45.claim: Qutb reports that two Companions would not part after meeting until one recited Surat al-Asr to the other, renewing their commitment to its guidance.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r45.anchor: كان الرجلان من أصحاب رسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] إذا التقيا لم يتفرقا حتى يقرأ أحدهما على الآخر سورة

RAZI-FULL:v32p80/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p80/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p80/r1.claim: One view takes العصر as time or the age; a report says the Prophet swore by time, but al-Razi refuses to treat its wording as Qur'an because that would invalidate prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v32p80/r1.anchor: ما روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه أقسم بالدهر

RAZI-FULL:v32p80/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p80/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p80/r2.claim: Time contains astonishing opposites such as health and illness or wealth and poverty, and resists a simple account of existence because past and future are absent while the indivisible present cannot be divided.

RAZI-FULL:v32p80/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p80/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p80/r3.claim: A final moment of life can redeem a wasted thousand years through repentance and eternal salvation, so time is among the greatest blessings.
RAZI-FULL:v32p80/r3.anchor: فلو ضيعت ألف سنة ، ثم تبث في اللمحة الأخيرة من العمر

RAZI-FULL:v32p80/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p80/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p80/r4.claim: Night and day are opportunities to remember and give thanks; the Qur'an also connects time and what occupies it to God's dominion.
RAZI-FULL:v32p80/r4.anchor: فلذلك أقسم به ونبه على أن الليل والنهار فرصة يضيعها المكلف

RAZI-FULL:v32p80/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p80/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p80/r5.claim: Arabs blamed misfortune on time, but the oath teaches that time is a blessing and the human being who wastes it is at fault.
RAZI-FULL:v32p80/r5.anchor: أنهم كانوا يضيفون الخسران إلى نوائت الدهر

RAZI-FULL:v32p81/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p81/r1.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v32p81/r1.claim: Abu Muslim reads العصر as one end of the day, the afternoon, paired with the morning's signs of resurrection, judgment, and the evening's signs of death and destruction.
RAZI-FULL:v32p81/r1.anchor: وهو قول أبي مسلم : المراد بالعصر أحد طرفي النهار

RAZI-FULL:v32p81/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p81/r2.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v32p81/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says afternoon signals that markets are closing: whoever has failed to earn must face dependents and creditors, a picture of the approaching Judgment and unprepared worldly life.
RAZI-FULL:v32p81/r2.anchor: قال الحسن رحمه الله : إنما أقسم بهذا الوقت

RAZI-FULL:v32p81/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p81/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v32p81/r3.claim: A prophetic report says that one who swears falsely after the afternoon prayer will face God's displeasure and lack of regard on Judgment Day.
RAZI-FULL:v32p81/r3.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : ( من حلف بعد العصر كاذبا

RAZI-FULL:v32p81/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p81/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p81/r4.claim: As midmorning in the previous sura assures the righteous of rising fortunes, the afternoon oath warns the doomed of decline; its remaining daylight urges repentance.
RAZI-FULL:v32p81/r4.anchor: فكما أقسم في حق الرابح بالضحى فكذا أقسم في حق الخاسر بالعصر

RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r1.claim: Muqatil says the oath is by the Asr prayer, citing the Hafsa recension of 2:238 and a reported reading of 5:106 as referring to Asr.
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r1.anchor: القول الثالث : وهو قول مقاتل : أراد صلاة العصر

RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r2.claim: A Prophetic report likens missing the Asr prayer to losing one's family and wealth, supporting its special merit.
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r2.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : ( من فاتته صلاة العصر فكأنما وتر أهله وماله )

RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r3.claim: One argument for the Asr interpretation is that people find it harder to pray as trade and livelihood occupy them late in the day.
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r3.anchor: لتهافت الناس في تجاراتهم ومكاسبهم آخر النهار واشتغالهم بمعايشهم

RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r4.claim: An unnamed report tells of a woman confessing adultery, killing her child in a vessel of vinegar, and selling it; the Prophet named penalties and linked the matter to abandoning Asr.
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r4.anchor: أما الزنا فعليك الرجم ، أما قتل الولد فجزاؤه جهنم

RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r5.claim: Asr closes the day's acts of worship like repentance closes deeds; swearing by it magnifies the prayer and urges its performance, through which loss becomes profit.
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r5.anchor: أن صلاة العصر بها يحصل ختم طاعات النهار ، فهي كالتوبة بها يختم الأعمال ، فكما تجب الوصية بالتوبة كذا بصلاة العصر

RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r6.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r6.claim: The Prophet says God will neither look at nor speak to three people on Judgment Day, including a man who lies under oath after Asr.
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r6.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( ثلاثة لا ينظر الله إليهم يوم القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r7.claim: Although prayer is a human act, God swears by it as a noble command He prescribed, not as our deed.
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r7.anchor: والجواب : أنه ليس قسما من حيث إنها فعلنا ، بل من حيث إنها أمر شريف تعبدنا الله تعالى بها

RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r8.claim: An unnamed fourth view takes the oath as referring to the era of the Messenger.
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r8.anchor: القول الرابع : أنه قسم بزمان الرسول عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r9.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r9.claim: A Prophetic parable compares workers hired from dawn to noon, noon to afternoon, and afternoon to sunset; the last group receives double pay, prompting the others' complaint and God's reply that this is His grace.
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r9.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : ( إنما مثلكم ومثل من كان قبلكم

RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r10.claim: Razi says the parable identifies the Prophet's era as the time assigned to him and his community; the oath can mean his era, alongside his place and lifespan (90:2; 15:72).
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r10.anchor: فهذا الخبر دل على أن العصر هو الزمان المختص به وبأمته

RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r11.claim: The Prophet and his community are like the setting in which events occur; since God honors that setting, their rejection of his call makes their loss and abandonment all the greater.
RAZI-FULL:v32p81#2/r11.anchor: فإذا وجب تعظيم حال الظرف فقس حال المظروف ، ثم وجه القسم ، كأنه تعالى يقول : أنت يا محمد حضرتهم ودعوتهم ، وهم أعرضوا عنك

STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r1.claim: Al-ʿAṣr is Makkan and likely follows Sūrah 94; ʿaṣr can mean late afternoon, its last hour, afternoon, the afternoon prayer, or an epoch.

STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r2.claim: Companions reportedly did not part after meeting until one recited the whole sūrah and greeted the other with peace.
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r2.anchor: whenever two Companions of the Prophet would meet they would not part company until one of them had recited al-ʿAṣr in its entirety

STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r3.claim: Read after Sūrah 102, ʿaṣr can mean time generally: vying for increase wastes it, and time's blessing is what people will be questioned about.
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r3.anchor: When viewed in relation to the previous sūrah, ʿaṣr can be understood as a reference to time in general, meaning that vying for increase (102:1) prevents people from spending their time

STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r4.claim: These three short verses can be seen as the whole Qur'an's message: humanity loses unless it turns to God.
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r4.anchor: From one perspective, these three short verses contain the entire message of the Quran, namely, that human beings are in loss unless they turn to God.

STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r5.speaker: al-Shāfiʿī
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r5.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī is reported to have said that if people pondered this sūrah, it would suffice them.
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r5.anchor: the famous legal scholar al-Shāfiʿī is reported to have said,“Were the people to ponder this sūrah, it would suffice them”

STUDYQURAN:103:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:1/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:1/r1.claim: ʿAṣr derives from ʿaṣara, “to squeeze,” and evokes time declining or fading quickly.
STUDYQURAN:103:1/r1.anchor: Linguistically, ʿaṣr derives from the verb ʿaṣara, meaning “to squeeze,” and thus relates to time that is declining or fading quickly.

STUDYQURAN:103:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:1/r2.speaker: many
STUDYQURAN:103:1/r2.claim: Many take it as the ʿaṣr prayer, identified with the “middlemost prayer” in 2:238, though that verse has other interpretations.
STUDYQURAN:103:1/r2.anchor: many judge the most likely to be the ʿaṣr prayer (Bḍ, Q, Z), which is considered to be the prayer referred to as the middlemost prayer in 2:238

STUDYQURAN:103:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:1/r3.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:103:1/r3.claim: Some understand ʿaṣr as the Prophet's era, blessed by the renewal of prophethood.
STUDYQURAN:103:1/r3.anchor: Some also say the term in this verse refers to the

STUDYQURAN:103:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:1/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:1/r4.claim: This reading applies to individuals and humanity's history: each generation falls a degree below the previous one.
STUDYQURAN:103:1/r4.anchor: the fall of humanity continues as the historical cycle unfolds, and each generation is a degree below the generation before it.

ASAD-NOTES:103:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:103:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:103:intro/r1.claim: The surah was revealed shortly after surah 94, Ash-Sharh.

ASAD-NOTES:103:1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:103:1/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:103:1/r1.claim: Unlike dahr, which denotes unlimited time without beginning or end, asr signifies passing time that cannot be recovered.
ASAD-NOTES:103:1/r1.anchor: dahr, which signifies "unlimited time", without beginning or end: i.e., "time absolute"). Hence, asr bears the connotation of the passing or the flight of time - time which can never be recaptured

ASAD-NOTES:103:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:103:1#n1/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:103:1#n1/r1.claim: Asr denotes measurable time made up of a succession of periods.
ASAD-NOTES:103:1#n1/r1.anchor: The term "asr denotes "time" that is measurable, consisting of a succession of periods

TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas takes al-asr as an hour during the day.
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {والعصر} [العصر: 1] قال: " العصر: ساعة من ساعات النهار "

TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r2.claim: Hasan interprets al-asr as the evening.

TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r3.claim: Al-Tabari says the word can mean time broadly, including the evening, night, and day, and does not restrict God's oath to only one sense of the word.
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r3.anchor: والعصر اسم للدهر، وهو العشي والليل والنهار، ولم يخصص مما شمله هذا الاسم معنى دون معنى

TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r5.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r5.claim: Ali is reported to recite an expanded reading that calls time ‘the vicissitudes of time’ and says humanity remains in loss until the end of time.
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r5.anchor: سمعت عليا، رضي الله عنه يقرأ هذا الحرف: «والعصر ونوائب الدهر، إن الإنسان لفي خسر، وإنه فيه إلى آخر الدهر»

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r1.claim: Arabic lexica offer competing senses for ʿaṣr: time or period, a time of day, morning, late afternoon or evening; the dual can mean day and night.
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Die arabischen Lexika verzeichnen eine Reihe von z. T. gegensätzlichen Bedeutungen

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r2.claim: Since other opening oaths name specific daytimes or night phases, ʿaṣr probably denotes a particular time rather than time in general.
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r2.anchor: stellt wohl auch ʿaṣr eine spezifische Zeitangabe dar und bezeichnet nicht allgemein „Zeitspanne“

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r3.speaker: Cuypers
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r3.claim: Cuypers reads ʿaṣr as a general span of time, though the commentator notes that he gives no further justification.
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r3.anchor: „Zeitspanne“ o. Ä. (so ohne weitere Begründung Cuypers 1999, 47)

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r4.claim: If ʿaṣr means late afternoon, this oath differs from all other early Meccan oaths naming night or stages of morning and forenoon.
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r4.anchor: Falls wirklich der Spätnachmittag intendiert ist, so hebt sich Q 103 von allen anderen frühmekkanischen Schwüren

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r5.claim: Qur'anic oaths likely draw on a characteristic pre-Islamic seer expression, a relationship that has not yet been adequately studied.
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r5.anchor: wahrscheinlichen, aber bis dato noch nicht hinreichend untersuchten Anlehnung an ein charakteristisches Ausdrucksmittel altarabischer Seher

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r6.speaker: Spitaler
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r6.claim: Medina II joins the oath verse to verse 2 in its verse division.
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r6.anchor: Medina II zieht V. 1 zu V. 2 (Spitaler, Verszählung, 72)

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r7.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r7.claim: Neuwirth treats the oath as an independent verse, in keeping with other sura-opening oaths.
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1:anmerkung/r7.anchor: Wie die anderen Schwüre am Surenanfang ist aber auch wa-l-ʿaṣr als eigenständiger Vers zu sehen (Neuwirth, Studien, 35)

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r1.claim: The three-rhyme sura is an opening single-member oath by late afternoon, followed by a rebuke; verse 3 exempts believers and differentiates good from bad people.
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r1.anchor: Die auf 3Kr reimende Sure besteht aus einem eingliedrigen Schwur „beim späten Nachmittag“ mit rügendem ʾinsān-Spruch als Schwuraussage
