CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r2.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r2.claim: Neuwirth argues that oaths by prayer times preserve the recipient's liturgical experience and give the sura a hymn-like tone.
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r2.anchor: Neuwirth schreibt Schwüren bei Tages- und Nachtzeiten allgemein die Funktion zu

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r3.claim: The commentator finds no hymn-like resonance in this sura and points to a critical discussion of Neuwirth's hypothesis elsewhere.
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r3.anchor: Eine solche hymnische Konnotation klingt jedoch im vorliegenden Text nirgends nach

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r4.speaker: Robinson
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r4.claim: Robinson's secular reading makes ʿaṣr the time when merchants count a day's earnings, linking the oath's image of profit to the eschatological loss in verse 2.
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r4.anchor: Robinsons profane Deutung des ʿaṣr als des Zeitpunkts, zu dem Händler am Ende eines Markttags ihre Einnahmen berechnen

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r6.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r6.claim: A prayer-time meaning for afternoon nevertheless remains possible.
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r6.anchor: dass mit dem Nachmittag doch eine Gebetszeit gemeint sein könnte (so Neuwirth, Frühmekkanische Suren, 157)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r16.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r16.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r16.claim: The exception here requires faith and good works, whereas al-ʿAṣr adds mutual exhortation to truth and patience; that added practice prevents further loss of reward.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r16.anchor: فلم يقل مثل ما قال في سورة العصر: {والعصر * إِنَّ الإنسان لَفِى خُسْرٍ * إِلاَّ الذين آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ الصالحات

TABATABAI:103:1-3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r1.claim: The surah condenses Quranic teachings and gathers its aims in the briefest statement; although it could be Meccan or Medinan, it seems more likely Meccan.
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r1.anchor: تخلص السورة جميع المعارف القرآنية وتجمع شتات مقاصد القرآن في أوجز بيان

TABATABAI:103:1-3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r2.claim: Given the next verses' universal loss except for those who follow truth and persevere, al-asr most fittingly means the Prophet's era, when Islam arose and truth appeared over falsehood.
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r2.anchor: والأنسب لما تتضمنه الآيتان التاليتان من شمول الخسران للعالم الإنساني إلا لمن اتبع الحق

TABATABAI:103:1-3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r3.speaker: unnamed view
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r3.claim: One interpretation takes al-asr as late afternoon, whose fading day, approaching night, and waning sun point to divine governance.
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r3.anchor: وقيل المراد به وقت العصر وهو الطرف الأخير من النهار لما فيه من الدلالة

TABATABAI:103:1-3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r4.speaker: unnamed view
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes al-asr as the afternoon prayer, the middle prayer and the best of the daily obligatory prayers.
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r4.anchor: وقيل المراد به صلاة العصر وهي الصلاة الوسطى التي هي أفضل الفرائض اليومية

TABATABAI:103:1-3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r5.speaker: unnamed view
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r5.claim: Some take al-asr as day and night, which are called the two asrs.
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r5.anchor: وقيل الليل والنهار ويطلق عليهما العصران

TABATABAI:103:1-3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r6.speaker: unnamed view
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r6.claim: Another reported meaning is time or the age, whose remarkable events indicate divine power.
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r6.anchor: وقيل الدهر لما فيه من عجائب الحوادث الدالة على القدرة الربوبية

TABATABAI:103:1-3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r7.speaker: unnamed reports
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r7.claim: Some narrations identify al-asr with the era of the Mahdi, when truth will fully prevail over falsehood.
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r7.anchor: وقد ورد في بعض الروايات أنه عصر ظهور المهدي عليه السلام لما فيه من تمام ظهور الحق

THALABI:v10p283#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p283#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p283#3/r1.claim: He says al-asr means time or the age.

THALABI:v10p283#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p283#3/r2.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v10p283#3/r2.claim: He says al-asr means night and day, also called the two asrs, or morning and evening, likewise called the two asrs; Humayd ibn Thawr’s poem witnesses the paired expression.
THALABI:v10p283#3/r2.anchor: ابن كيسان: الليل والنهار ويقال لهما: العصران وللغداة والعشي أيضا: عصران

THALABI:v10p283#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p283#3/r3.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p283#3/r3.claim: He says al-asr is the time from noon until sunset.
THALABI:v10p283#3/r3.anchor: الحسن: بعد زوال الشمس إلى غروبها

THALABI:v10p283#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p283#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p283#3/r4.claim: He interprets it as the final hour of the day.
THALABI:v10p283#3/r4.anchor: قتادة: آخر ساعة من ساعات النهار

THALABI:v10p283#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p283#3/r5.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v10p283#3/r5.claim: He identifies al-asr as the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer.

THALABI:v10p283#3/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p283#3/r13.speaker: علي
THALABI:v10p283#3/r13.claim: One reading attributed to Ali adds that a person remains in loss until the end of time.
THALABI:v10p283#3/r13.anchor: قال: [كان علي رضي الله عنه يقرأ ذلك] : إن الإنسان لفي خسر وإنه فيه إلى آخر الدهر

THALABI:v10p283#3/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p283#3/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
THALABI:v10p283#3/r14.claim: The same reading is attributed to Ibn Masud, extending the state of loss to the end of time.
THALABI:v10p283#3/r14.anchor: وكذلك هي في قراءة ابن مسعود

THALABI:v10p283#3/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p283#3/r15.speaker: علي
THALABI:v10p283#3/r15.claim: Another reading attributed to Ali renders al-asr as the vicissitudes of time and adds that the person remains in loss until time’s end.
THALABI:v10p283#3/r15.anchor: وكان علي يقرأها: والعصر، ونوائب الدهر، إن الإنسان لفي خسر، وإنه فيه إلى آخر الدهر

THALABI:v10p283#3/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p283#3/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p283#3/r16.claim: The sound reading is the one followed by the general reciters and standard codices.
THALABI:v10p283#3/r16.anchor: والقراءة الصحيحة ما عليه العامة والمصاحف

THALABI:v10p283#3/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p283#3/r17.speaker: أبي بن كعب
THALABI:v10p283#3/r17.claim: Ubayy says he recited the surah to the Prophet and asked him for its interpretation.
THALABI:v10p283#3/r17.anchor: عن أبي أمامة عن أبي بن كعب قال: قرأت على رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) والعصر فقلت:

THALABI:v10p284/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p284/r1.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v10p284/r1.claim: The Prophet says al-asr is an oath by God on behalf of the audience at the day’s end; he identifies the person in loss with Abu Jahl and the believers, righteous deeds, truth, and patience in turn with Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali.
THALABI:v10p284/r1.anchor: فقال: «والعصر قسم من الله أقسم لكم بآخر النهار» إن الإنسان لفي خسر قال: «أبو جهل بن هشام»

THALABI:v10p284/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p284/r2.speaker: علي بن عبد الله بن عباس
THALABI:v10p284/r2.claim: While preaching from the Prophet’s pulpit, he recited the surah and repeated the same identifications of Abu Jahl, Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali with its phrases.
THALABI:v10p284/r2.anchor: فوافيت علي بن عبد الله بن عباس يخطب على منبر رسول الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets al-asr as time or the ages.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r2.claim: Al-Farra says al-asr is time, by which God swears.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r2.anchor: قال الفراء: هو (¬5) الدهر أقسم الله به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r3.claim: Qatada interprets it as the last hour of the daytime.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r3.anchor: قال (¬7) قتادة: أراد آخر ساعة من ساعات النهار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r4.claim: A report from Mujahid on Ibn Abbas's authority says al-asr is the part of the day near sunset.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r4.anchor: وهو رواية مجاهد عن ابن عباس قال: العصر ما يلي المغرب # من النهار (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r5.speaker: ابن كيسان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r5.claim: Ibn Kaysan says it means night and day; the commentators also hold this view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r5.anchor: قال (¬2) ابن كيسان: هو الليل والنهار (¬3). وهذا قول المفسرين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r6.claim: The meanings of time, day, night, morning, and evening are all valid in Arabic usage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r6.anchor: والعصر بهذه (¬5) المعاني صحيح في اللغة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r7.speaker: ابن السكيت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r7.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit cites poetry using al-asr in the sense of time or an age.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r7.anchor: أنشد ابن السكيت (¬7): ثم اتقى وأي عصر يتقى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r8.claim: Arabic uses al-asr for the day, night, morning, and evening.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r8.anchor: ويقال لليوم، والليلة، والغداة، والعشي: العصر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r9.speaker: حميد بن ثور
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r9.claim: Humayd ibn Thawr's poetic dual al-asran refers to day and night.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r9.anchor:
قال حميد بن ثور:
 ولن يلبث العصران يوم وليلة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r10.speaker: ابن السكيت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r10.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit cites a line with al-asrayn and explains it as morning and evening.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r10.anchor:
أنشد (¬2) ابن السكيت:
 وأمطله العصرين حتى يملني

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r11.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r11.claim: Al-Layth says al-asr means evening, a usage from which the afternoon prayer takes its name.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r11.anchor:
قال الليث: والعصر العشي، وأنشد:
 تروح بنا يا عمر ...
وقد قصر العصر (¬6)
قال: وبه سميت صلاة (العصر) (¬7) (¬8)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r12.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r12.claim: The scholars of meaning find a lesson in the passage of night and day: day declines as night arrives.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p293#2/r12.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني في "العصر" بجميع هذه المعاني عبرة للناظرة من جهة مرور الليل والنهار

WAHIDI-QT:103:1/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:103:1/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:103:1/r1.claim: Al-asr is time, by which God swears.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:103:1-3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:103:1-3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:103:1-3/r1.claim: Al-ʿAṣr means time, by which God swears.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:103:1-3/r1.anchor: { والعصر } هو الدهر، أقسم الله به.

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r1.claim: The rendering says: By the age; humankind is in absolute loss, except those who believe, do righteous works, counsel one another to truth, and counsel patience.
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r1.anchor: Kasem olsun ki asra (1) insan mutlak bir hüsranda (2)

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r2.claim: The opening waw marks an oath, as in Wad-Duha.

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r3.claim: As a noun, asr can mean the whole age, day and night, parts of the day, afternoon prayer or time, a group, and rain; as a verb it can mean restraining, preventing, taxing, or squeezing out juice.
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r3.anchor: Kāmûs’ta zikrolunduğu üzere “asr” kelimesi lügatta isim olarak dehr

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r4.claim: Vocalization variants asr, isr, and usr can mark a specific time; paired asran can refer to day and night or morning and evening.
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r4.anchor: Gündüzle geceye ve sabah ile akşama “asrân” denilir.

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r5.claim: With the generic article, al-asr may include every sense; with the covenant article, it may identify one particular time.
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r5.anchor: Lâm-ı cins ile وَٱلْعَصْرِ makāmına göre bunların her birinin cinsine

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r6.claim: In Turkish usage asr commonly means time generally, the present era, or a period of eighty or a hundred years.
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r6.anchor: Ondan dolayı lisânımızda “asr” mutlak zaman ve bilhassa içinde bulunulan zaman

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r7.claim: Exegetes propose afternoon prayer, afternoon time, the age or time generally, Muhammad's era, and the end times.
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r7.anchor: müfessirîn başlıca ikindi namazı, ikindi vakti, dehr ve zaman, bâhusus asr-ı Muhammedî

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r8.speaker: İbn Cerîr
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r8.claim: Ibn Jarir holds that asr is broad enough to include all its lexical senses, since the verse gives no reason to select one; the author endorses this inclusive reading.
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r8.anchor: Bu hususta savab olan kavil şudur: Rabbimiz teâlâ asra kasem etmiştir

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r9.speaker: Mukātil
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r9.claim: Muqatil says Allah swears by the afternoon prayer, whose special merit follows from the majority's identification of the middle prayer as asr.
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r9.anchor: Mukātil demiştir ki: Allah teâlâ ikindi namazına kasem buyurmuştur

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r10.claim: Prophetic reports call the delayed middle prayer the asr prayer and warn that missing asr is like losing one's family and property.
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r10.anchor: Hendek vak‘asında Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm شَغَلُونَا عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ الْوُسْطَى صَلاَةِ الْعَصْرِ buyurmuştu

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r11.claim: Afternoon prayer is especially attention-awakening because it interrupts the period when people are most absorbed in work and trade.
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r11.anchor: gündüzün âhiri olmak hasebiyle dünyada diğer mahlûkāt ve hayvânâtın yaratılışından

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r12.speaker: Katâde
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r12.claim: Qatada says Allah swears by afternoon time as a counterpart to duha, with signs of divine power.
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r12.anchor: Katâde demiştir ki: İkindi namazının vakti olmak ve “duhâ”ya mukabil birtakım delâil-i kudreti hâvî bulunmak

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r13.claim: Afternoon evokes humanity's creation late in the world's day, the closing period of human life, and the sorrow of returning without gain; this complements the previous surah's warning about rivalry.
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r13.anchor: dünyada bir gün mesabesinde demek olan insan ömrünün de son demlerini andırdığı

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r14.claim: Dehr, in Raghib's definition, is the interval from the universe's beginning to its end; zaman can name that whole or any part, while dehr also means long duration, remaining lifetime, or lifespan.

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r15.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits Ali's interpretive recitation: by time and its calamities, humankind remains in loss until time's end.
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r15.anchor: İbn Cerîr’in rivayet ettiği vechile Hazret-i Ali radıyallâhu anh’tan وَالْعَصْرِ وَنـَوَائِبِ الدَّهْرِ

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r16.claim: This reading interprets asr as dehr, whose recurring calamities and changes warn people and whose loss continues to the end; squeezing or confinement may also reinforce the loss side.
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r16.anchor: İbn Cerîr’in rivayet ettiği vechile Hazret-i Ali radıyallâhu anh’tan

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r17.claim: Another view says dehr contains every wonder that displays the Creator's power, where ordinary and extraordinary events, blessings, disasters, gains, and losses unfold.
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r17.anchor: Demek ki “asr”, dehr mânasınadır ve dehre kasemin hikmeti de onun insana

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r18.speaker: Râzî
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r18.claim: Razi presents time as puzzling: it is divisible into past, present, and future, yet the present is indivisible and past and future are nonexistent, so time seems neither simply existent nor nonexistent.

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r19.claim: Philosophers and theologians have debated whether time exists, is nonexistent or imagined, and whether our knowledge of it is immediate or abstracted.
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r19.anchor: Râzî derki “akıl ona yok diye hükmedemez; çünkü devirler

ELMALILI:103:1-3/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r20.claim: A cited Arab poet compares time to a ship carrying people toward death while its movement remains unseen.
ELMALILI:103:1-3/r20.anchor: Onun için felâsife ve mütekellimîn zaman mevcud mudur, ma‘dum mudur, mevhum mudur

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r1.claim: Time gathers every kind of change, benefit, harm, and wonder; the oath draws attention to how people fare in gain or loss within it.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r1.anchor: Zaman böyle varlıkla yokluk arasında nîk ü bed, ni‘met ü nikmet, serra vü darrâ

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r2.claim: Human life is precious capital; each unprofitable instant wastes it, but a final righteous act may make up for years of waste and win eternal paradise.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r2.anchor: İnsanın ömrü en kıymetli sermayesidir. Ne kazanacaksa onunla kazanacaktır

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r3.claim: Sufis say a person should be the child of the moment: value the present and use it to gain good for the afterlife.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r3.anchor: sûfiyye, “sûfî ibnü’l-vakt olmalıdır; yani ömrünün ve bilhassa fiilen içinde bulunduğu vakt-i hâlin

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r4.claim: People who deny the afterlife also urge seizing the present for worldly pleasure, though their aim differs from the Sufi's afterlife-oriented use of time.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r4.anchor: gün bugündür, saat bu saattir, ne yapacaksak şimdi yapmalıyız” diyerek herçibâdâbad vaktine

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r5.claim: Time is the opportunity for action, whether productive or wasteful, profitable or harmful; the oath highlights the value and nature of life's moments.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r5.anchor: İşte vakit böyle bir fırsat ve ömür bütün ânâtıyla böyle kâr ve zarara mâruz bir sermaye

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r6.claim: Time's senses of restraint and bestowal can support both the loss side and the exception of those who gain through faith and good works.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r6.anchor: asrın dehr ü zaman mânası mülâhaza olunurken men‘ve atâ mânalarına da işaret edilmiş bulunduğu hafî değildir

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r7.claim: A cited couplet says each passing day takes away part of the speaker, since nothing is more precious than life.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r7.anchor: “Her gün geçtikçe benim birazım gider, benim için ise

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r8.claim: People fail to calculate what they gained against the life they spent and wrongly imagine that passing time means they are growing.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r8.anchor: insan geçen cüz’ünün yerine ne kazandığını hesab etmez de gün geçtikçe büyüdüğünü zu‘m eder

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r9.claim: A poem says people rejoice at days passing although each one reduces their remaining lifespan.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r9.anchor: Biz günleri geçiriyoruz diye ferahlanıyoruz, hâlbuki her geçen gün ecelden, ömürden bir eksikliktir

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r10.claim: The oath warns that time consumes life and leaves people in loss unless they believe and do good works.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r10.anchor: o geçen leyl ü nehar vücûdunu kemirmekte ve bu suretle o her dem hüsran içinde kalmaktadır

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r11.claim: In an elegy for his teacher and the Balkan War dead, the author portrays life as deceiving people while death draws its nourishment and each breath weaves shrouds.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r11.anchor: إِنَّ الْحَيَاةَ تَغُرُّنَا وَمَ مَاتُنَا مِنْ ضَرْعِهَا يَسْتَرْضِعُ الأَْلْبَانَ

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r12.claim: People wrongly blame time for their misfortunes; a cited poem says time is not corrupt, but people themselves are.

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r13.claim: The oath honors time as a valuable blessing and says those who fail to work toward reform are themselves in loss.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r13.anchor: Haddizâtında asrın, zamanın aybı, kabahati, zararı yoktur, o değerli bir nimettir

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r14.claim: The warning against blaming time is connected to the hadith forbidding people to curse time.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r14.anchor: hadîs-i şerîfiyle[^26] işaret olunan mânadır. Bu tafsîlâttan anlaşılır ki asrı

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r15.claim: Swearing by asr honors time and avoids the materialist implication of saying wa-al-dahr, recalling those who claimed that only time destroys.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r15.anchor: daha sarih olmak için وَالدّهْرِ denilmeyip de وَٱلْعَصْرِ buyurulması

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r16.claim: The definite article first directs hearers to the time closest to them; with the Prophet as first audience, this suggests the Prophetic era.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r16.anchor: muhataplara yakından alâkası olan asrı düşündürmek lâzım gelir

ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r17.claim: The Muhammadic era is the most immediate sense of asr while also including the broader temporal meanings.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#2/r17.anchor: Bu asırdan murad, asr-ı nübüvvet, yani asr-ı Muhammedî olmak tebâdür eder

ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r1.claim: The first Prophetic-era phase began with Muhammad's mission amid religious disorder, extinguished guidance, and widespread ignorance, disbelief, injustice, and corruption.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r1.anchor: nübüvvet, fazilet, hakk u adalet, ma‘rifetullah

ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r2.claim: The Qur'an began descending with the command iqra on a Night of Power, and prophetic light rose to call humanity toward reform, paradise, and divine approval.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r2.anchor: bir leyle-i kadirde اِقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ emriyle Kur’an nâzil olarak nûr-ı nübüvvet tulû‘etmişti

ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r3.claim: As discussed in Surat al-Bayyina, spreading the upright religion called people away from total loss and began transformations that led from the middle ages to the last era.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r3.anchor: لَمْ يَكُن Sûresi’nde geçtiği üzere dîn-i kayyimenin neşriyle insanlığı şerrü’l-beriyyenin istîlâsından

ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r4.claim: The oath by this era before the declaration that humanity is in loss except believers and doers of good carries important meaning.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#3/r4.anchor: O vakit bu asra kasem ederek إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r1.claim: The Prophetic era from the mission to Muhammad's death had two phases: struggle, then conquest and victory, as prophetic light spread guidance and distinguished truth from falsehood.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r1.anchor: ki biri mücahede, biri de feth ü nusret ile

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r2.claim: The Muhammadic era from the Hijra through the end of time encompasses later centuries and fulfills the effects and aims of all earlier prophetic eras.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r2.anchor: hicret-i seniyyeden ilâ âhiri’d-dehr bütün kurûn-ı ahîreyi ihtivâ eden âhir zamandır

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r3.claim: The author and some exegetes find the Muhammadic era the most comprehensive and immediate meaning of asr.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r3.anchor: müfessirînin dediği gibi bizce de en ziyade mütebâdir olan bu asırdır

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r4.claim: Qur'anic history is divided into the eras before Moses' Torah, from the Torah to the final Prophet, and the final era of Muhammad and his community.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r4.anchor: zamanın üç kısma taksîmine işaret olunmuştu

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r5.claim: A day analogy portrays the Muhammadic era as the afternoon of human history, following earlier ages as afternoon follows morning and noon.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r5.anchor: asr-ı Muhammedî bugünün ikindisi misâlinde temsil edilmiştir

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r6.claim: A hadith compares prior peoples' work periods to morning and midday, and the Muslim community's work from asr to sunset, for which God grants twice the wage after the Jews and Christians object.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r6.anchor: Sizden evvel geçmişlere nisbetle sizin vaktiniz, ikindi namazıyla gurûb-ı şems arası kadardır

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r7.claim: Some exegetes use this hadith to identify asr with the time of the Prophet and the community praised as the best brought forth for humanity.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r7.anchor: Bir kısım müfessirîn bu hadis ile istidlâl ederek demişlerdir ki: Bu hadis

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r8.claim: As Allah swore by the Prophet's location and life, this surah swears by his era.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r8.anchor: diye mekânına ve لَعَمْرُكَ [el-Hicr 15/72] diye ömrüne kasem buyurduğu gibi burada da asrına kasem buyurmuştur

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r9.claim: The oath encompasses every meaning of asr, especially the final era as the afternoon of time and the age of Muhammad, before the declaration that humankind is in loss.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r9.anchor: Her mânasıyla asra ve bâhusus pek büyük hâdisâta

ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r14.speaker: Ebû Medîne
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r14.claim: He reports that two of the Prophet's Companions would not part after meeting until they recited Sūrat al-ʿAṣr to each other and then exchanged greetings.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r14.anchor: Ebû Medîne’den[^57]-ki sohbeti vardır- şöyle dediğini rivayet eylemişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r1.claim: Asr can denote absolute or present time, a generation or ruler's era, night, morning, evening, afternoon, the afternoon prayer, or a religious period.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r1.anchor: Asr (asır) kelimesi isim olarak “mutlak zaman, içinde bulunulan zaman, karn (80 veya 100 yıllık zaman dilimi)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r2.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r2.claim: Commentators have read asr as afternoon, the afternoon prayer, absolute time, Muhammad's era, or the end times.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r2.anchor: Müfessirler burada zikredilen asr kelimesini ikindi vakti, ikindi namazı, mutlak zaman

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r3.claim: The commentary prefers absolute time as the meaning best suited to the surah's content and message.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r3.anchor: Bize göre bunlar içinde sûrenin içeriğine ve mesajına en uygun düşeni “mutlak zaman” anlamıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r4.claim: The oath by time calls attention to its place and importance in human life and as the arena where God's acts manifest His existence and boundless power.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r4.anchor: Zamana yemin edilerek onun insan hayatındaki yerine ve önemine dikkat çekilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r5.claim: For humans, time is the condition of life and a field of opportunity in which they can carry out every kind of action.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r5.anchor: insan bakımından da hayatını içinde geçirdiği ve her türlü eylemlerini gerçekleştirebildiği bir imkân ve fırsatlar alanıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r6.claim: God swears by this precious reality to stress time's value and warn that a person who fails to use it well ends in loss.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r6.anchor: zamanın önemine dikkat çekmiş; onu iyi değerlendirmeyen insanın sonunun

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r17.claim: Despite its brevity, Surah al-Asr contains a rich summary of the Qur'an's religious and moral duties and counsels.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r17.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’deki bütün dinî ve ahlâkî yükümlülüklerin, öğütlerin özü sayılmaya değer

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r18.speaker: İmam Şâfiî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r18.claim: Al-Shafi'i is quoted as saying that this short surah alone would suffice humanity if nothing else had been revealed, since it embraces all Qur'anic sciences.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r18.anchor: Şayet Kur’an’da başka bir şey nâzil olmasaydı, şu pek kısa sûre bile insanlara yeterdi. Bu sûre Kur’an’ın bütün ilimlerini kucaklıyor

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r19.speaker: Mehmet Âkif Ersoy
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r19.claim: Akif's poem presents true faith, righteous conduct, truth, and steadfastness as the sequence that saves humanity from loss.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r19.anchor: Başta îmân-ı hakîkî geliyor sonra salâh Sonra hak sonra sebât: İşte kuzum insanlık Dördü birleşti mi yoktur sana hüsrân artık

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r20.speaker: Mehmet Âkif Ersoy
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r20.claim: Akif's poem says the Companions would recite Surah al-Asr when they were about to part.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r20.anchor: Hani ashâb-ı kirâm ayrılalım derlerken Mutlaka sûre-i ve’l-Asr’ı okurmuş

BURSEVI:v10p390#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p390#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p390#3/r1.claim: The loss is grave because the servant sins against the Lord and against immense benefaction; the indefinite form may also mark a distinctive kind of loss beyond ordinary human usage.
BURSEVI:v10p390#3/r1.anchor: والذنب يعظم إما لعظم من في حقه الذنب أو لأنه في مقابلة النعمة العظيمة

QASHANI:103:3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:103:3/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:103:3/r1.claim: Time is the duration of the temporal world and its source; people wrongly treat it as the agent of change, while God is the true agent manifest through it.
QASHANI:103:3/r1.anchor: أقسم بالعصر أي: بامتداد بقاء الزمان وما فيه وما يحدث معه بمبدعه وعلته الذي هو الدهر.

QASHANI:103:3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:103:3/r2.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
QASHANI:103:3/r2.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying not to revile time, since God is time; Qashani gives no grading.
QASHANI:103:3/r2.anchor: لا تسبوا الدهر فإن الله هو الدهر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p528/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p528/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p528/r1.claim: The oath by time confirms the statement, as Qur'anic oaths do, and its object is a sign of God's wondrous creation, power, and knowledge.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p528/r1.anchor: أقسم الله تعالى بالعصر قسما يراد به تأكيد الخبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p528/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p528/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p528/r2.claim: “Time” has several possible referents; whichever is intended, its significance comes from being a period that manifests divine action, by contextual indication, addition, or shared reference.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p528/r2.anchor: وللعصر معانن يتعين أن يكون المراد منها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p528/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p528/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p528/r3.claim: Its common sense is the late afternoon, from when a body's shadow equals its noon shadow to twice that amount, through yellowing sunlight before evening; the poem by al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza uses ʿaṣran for that late time.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p528/r3.anchor: وأشهر إطلاق لفظ العصر أنه علم بالغلبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p528/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p528/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p528/r4.claim: The afternoon reminds one of the solar-earth system and recurring day-night cycle, the end of daily work and social rhythms, household life, blessings, and the approach of death after life's stages.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p528/r4.anchor: وفيه إيماء إلى التذكير بمثل الحياة حين تدنو آجال الناس بعد مضي أطوار الشباب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p480/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p480/r2.speaker: مالك عن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p480/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam defines al-Asr as evening, though Ibn Kathir says the first view is the well-known one.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p480/r2.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم: هو العشي، والمشهور الأول.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r5.claim: The generic definite al-nafs parallels generic human statements qualified by exceptions; the verse forbids killing any protected life, Muslim or treaty-holder, except for a legally valid cause.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r5.anchor: وهذه الآية نهي عن قتل النفس المحرمة، مؤمنة كانت أو معاهدة إلا بالحق

RAZI-FULL:v32p85/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p85/r8.speaker: سلام بن المنذر
RAZI-FULL:v32p85/r8.claim: A report has Salām ibn al-Mundhir reading al-ʿaṣr with a kasra on ṣād; al-Rāzī attributes it to stopping for breath or another impediment, not to carrying pause into liaison.
RAZI-FULL:v32p85/r8.anchor: ما يروى عن سلام بن المنذر أنه قرأ ، والعصر بكسر الصاد ولعله وقف لانقطاع نفس أو لعارض منعه من إدراج القراءة

TABRISI:103:3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:103:3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:103:3/r1.claim: The root of ʿaṣr means squeezing cloth to extract water; the term came to mean a time in which events can be pressed or late afternoon. Poems illustrate “the two ʿaṣrs” as morning/evening and night/day.
TABRISI:103:3/r1.anchor: أصل العصر عصر الثوب ونحوه وهو فتله لإخراج مائه

TABRISI:103:3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:103:3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، الكلبي، الجبائي
TABRISI:103:3/r3.claim: They say the oath is by time, whose alternating nights and days provide a lesson for perceptive people.
TABRISI:103:3/r3.anchor: أقسم سبحانه بالدهر لأن فيه عبرة لذوي الأبصار

TABRISI:103:3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:103:3/r4.speaker: الحسن، قتادة
TABRISI:103:3/r4.claim: They identify the oath as late afternoon, the day's final edge as the sun sets and night arrives; this complements the oath by forenoon, and both times are revered by the adherents of the two religions.
TABRISI:103:3/r4.anchor: هو وقت العشي عن الحسن وقتادة فعلى هذا أقسم سبحانه بالطرف الأخير من النهار

TABRISI:103:3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:103:3/r5.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:103:3/r5.claim: Maqātil says the oath is by the mid-afternoon prayer, the middle prayer.
TABRISI:103:3/r5.anchor: أقسم بصلاة العصر وهي الصلاة الوسطى عن مقاتل

TABRISI:103:3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:103:3/r6.speaker: ابن كيسان
TABRISI:103:3/r6.claim: Ibn Kaysān takes ʿaṣr as night and day, together called the two ʿaṣrs.
TABRISI:103:3/r6.anchor: هو الليل والنهار ويقال لهما العصران عن ابن كيسان

ALUSI-FULL:v30p227/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وابن الزبير والجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227/r1.claim: They classify Surat al-ʿAsr as Meccan; Mujahid, Qatada, and Muqatil are cited for classifying it as Medinan, and its three verses are undisputed.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227/r1.anchor: مكية في قول ابن عباس وابن الزبير والجمهور ومدنية في قول مجاهد وقتادة ومقاتل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p227/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227/r2.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227/r2.claim: Al-Shafiʿi is reported to say that even if no other surah had been revealed, this one would suffice because it contains the Qurʾan’s sciences.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227/r2.anchor: انه قال لو لم ينزل غير هذه السورة لكفت الناس لانها شملت جميع علوم القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v30p227/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227/r3.speaker: أبو حذيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227/r3.claim: He reports that two Companions would recite Surat al-ʿAsr to one another whenever they met, parting only after one recited it and the other greeted him.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227/r3.anchor: كان الرجلان من اصحاب رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم اذا التقيا لم يفترقا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p227/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227/r4.claim: The surah follows al-Takathur because it points to those whom worldly rivalry did not distract.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p227/r4.anchor: وفيها اشارة إلى حال من لم يلهه التكاثر ولذا وضعت بعد سورته

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p415/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p415/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p415/r3.claim: The form is unique in the Quran; its root also appears in al-ʿAsr, Yusuf’s dream and the harvest year, and the whirlwind in al-Baqara.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p416/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p416/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p416/r4.claim: The author derives ʿasr meaning time from human life being pressed through trials and hardship; she rejects al-Raghib’s derivation from what remains after squeezing.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p416/r4.anchor: ملحوظ فيه أنه يستخلص عصارة الإنسان بالضغط والابتلاء والمعاناة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p245/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p245/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p245/r1.claim: She questions the link between the supposed greatness of night and day and the claim that human striving differs, and between the falling star and the assertion that the Prophet is neither astray nor deluded.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p245/r1.anchor: بين: إن سعيكم لشتى؟ أو بين عظمة النجم إذا هوى، و {مَا ضَلَّ صَاحِبُكُمْ وَمَا غَوَى} ؟

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p251/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p251/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p251/r2.claim: The oath by Time evokes human beings being crushed and refined under pressure; Time extracts their essence and exposes their worth, explaining loss or salvation in the next verses.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p251/r2.anchor: الواو في موضعها الذي تطرد به الظاهرة الأسلوبية في اللفت إلى ابتلاء الإنسان بالزمن يعصره ويصهره بالضغط والمعاناة

NASHR:v1p261#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p261#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p261#2/r1.claim: Among readers of Hamza, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Yaʿqub, and Warsh who join surahs, many choose a brief pause at four specified transitions, including Fajr and Asr.
NASHR:v1p261#2/r1.anchor: اختار كثير منهم لهم السكت بين (المدثر، ولا أقسم بيوم القيامة - وبين - الانفطار وويل للمصلين

NASHR:v1p261#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p261#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p261#2/r2.claim: Many of the same named readers who pause generally choose basmala at the four transitions; the author lists Ibn Ghalbun, the Hidaya author, Makki, and others.
NASHR:v1p261#2/r2.anchor: وكذا الآخذون بالسكت لمن ذكر من أبي عمرو، وابن عامر، ويعقوب، وورش، اختار كثير منهم لهم البسملة

NASHR:v1p261#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p261#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p261#2/r3.claim: They separate the joins to avoid jarring phrases such as أهل المغفرة لا, ادخلي جنتي لا, لله ويل, and وتواصوا بالصبر ويل.
NASHR:v1p261#2/r3.anchor: وإنما اختاروا ذلك لبشاعة وقوع مثل ذلك إذا قيل: (أهل المغفرة لا) أو: (ادخلي جنتي لا)

NASHR:v1p261#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p261#2/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p261#2/r4.claim: Readers who join cannot insert basmala where explicit transmission excludes it, since that would oppose the transmitted reading with a discretionary choice.
NASHR:v1p261#2/r4.anchor: ولم يمكنهم البسملة له ; لأنه ثبت عنه النص بعدم البسملة، فلو بسملوا لصادموا النص بالاختيار

NASHR:v1p261#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p261#2/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p261#2/r5.claim: Most authorities make no special distinction for these four transitions; this is the position of Faris ibn Ahmad, Ibn Sufyan, Abu al-Tahir, the Iraqis, al-Dani, and other investigators.
NASHR:v1p261#2/r5.anchor: والأكثرون على عدم التفرقة بين الأربعة وغيرها

NASHR:v1p261#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p261#2/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p261#2/r6.claim: The special treatment derives from the reader's general practice: special sakt means joining elsewhere, while special basmala means pausing elsewhere; no one transmits basmala for those who join.
NASHR:v1p261#2/r6.anchor: تخصيص السكت والبسملة في الأربعة المذكورة مفرع على الوصل والسكت مطلقا

BURHAN:v1p100/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p100/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p100/r8.claim: The one-word openings of al-Tur, al-Rahman, al-Haqqa, al-Qari'a, and al-Asr are counted by analogy with al-Fajr and al-Duha for rhyme, though their quantities differ.
BURHAN:v1p100/r8.anchor: ﴿ والطور ﴾ و ﴿ الرحمن ﴾ و ﴿ الحاقة ﴾ و ﴿ القارعة ﴾ و ﴿ والعصر ﴾ حملا على

BURHAN:v1p179#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p179#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p179#2/r1.claim: Fifteen sūras open with an oath, including al-Fajr and al-Asr; this is the fifth listed mode of sūra opening.
BURHAN:v1p179#2/r1.anchor: الخامس القسم نحو ﴿ والصافات ﴾ ﴿ والذاريات ﴾ ﴿ والطور ﴾ ﴿ والنجم ﴾

BURHAN:v1p267/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p267/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p267/r4.claim: A word is a single utterance, potentially two to ten letters; al-Fajr, al-Duha, and al-Asr can each be a one-word verse, as can some opening letters for Kufans.
BURHAN:v1p267/r4.anchor: وأما الكلمة فهى اللفظة الواحدة وقد تكون على حرفين مثل ما ولى وله ولك

BURHAN:v2p34/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p34/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p34/r1.claim: Al-Asr is listed among thirty-one sūras containing both abrogating and abrogated material.

ITQAN:v1p37/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p37/r2.speaker: عكرمة والحسن بن أبي الحسن
ITQAN:v1p37/r2.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits from Ikrima and al-Hasan that al-Fajr and al-Asr are among the surahs revealed in Mecca; he also lists surahs revealed in Medina.
ITQAN:v1p37/r2.anchor: وقال البيهقي في دلائل النبوة أنبأنا أبو عبد الله الحافظ أخبرنا أبو محمد بن زياد العدل

ITQAN:v1p77#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p77#2/r5.speaker: جابر بن زيد
ITQAN:v1p77#2/r5.claim: Jabir ibn Zayd's reported Meccan revelation order places al-Fajr tenth and al-ʿAsr thirteenth.
ITQAN:v1p77#2/r5.anchor: عن جابر بن زيد قال أول ما أنزل الله من القرآن بمكة

ITQAN:v1p176/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p176/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
ITQAN:v1p176/r1.claim: The reported order of Ibn Masʿud's codex places al-Fajr and al-ʿAsr among the mufassal sūras, with al-Fajr preceding al-ʿAsr.
ITQAN:v1p176/r1.anchor: تأليف مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود الطوال البقرة والنساء وآل عمران

ITQAN:v3p57/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p57/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p57/r2.claim: Al-Suyuti says this four-part classification of sūras according to abrogation is open to question, as later discussion shows.
ITQAN:v3p57/r2.anchor: كذا قال وفيه نظر يعرف مما سيأتي

ITQAN:v3p282/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p282/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p282/r1.claim: Al-Suyuti says all sūras begin in one of ten forms of speech; the oath is the fifth form and opens fifteen sūras.
ITQAN:v3p282/r1.anchor: افتتح سور القرآن بعشرة أنواع من الكلام لا يخرج شيء من السور عنها

ITQAN:v3p282/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p282/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p282/r3.claim: The oath by al-ʿAsr refers either to the day's latter part or to time as a whole.
ITQAN:v3p282/r3.anchor: العصر بالشطر الآخر أو بجملة الزمان

ITQAN:v4p353/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p353/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p353/r5.claim: A fifth pattern pairs an oath with a proposition about human action or condition; al-ʿAsr exemplifies it by declaring humanity in loss.

ITQAN:v1p65/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p65/r1.speaker: ابن حبيب
ITQAN:v1p65/r1.claim: Ibn Habib says most of the Qur'an was revealed during daytime, while examples of night revelation were separately collected.
ITQAN:v1p65/r1.anchor: قال ابن حبيب نزل أكثر القرآن نهارا وأما الليل فتتبعت له أمثلة

ITQAN:v1p180/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p180/r1.speaker: الجعبري
ITQAN:v1p180/r1.claim: Al-Jaʿbari defines an āya as Qur'an composed of sentences, explicitly or implicitly, with a beginning or ending within a sūra; its name signifies a mark.
ITQAN:v1p180/r1.anchor: قال الجعبري حد الآية قرآن مركب من جمل ولو تقديرا ذو مبدإ أو مقطع

ITQAN:v1p180/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p180/r2.speaker: غيره
ITQAN:v1p180/r2.claim: Another definition calls an āya a portion of the Qur'an separated from what precedes and follows it.
ITQAN:v1p180/r2.anchor: وقال غيره الآية طائفة من القرآن منقطعة عما قبلها وما بعدها

ITQAN:v1p180/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p180/r3.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v1p180/r3.claim: Another explanation calls each counted unit an āya because it proves the messenger's truth and the challengers' inability.
ITQAN:v1p180/r3.anchor: وقيل هي الواحدة من المعدودات في السور سميت به لأنها علامة على صدق من أتى بها

ITQAN:v1p180/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p180/r4.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v1p180/r4.claim: A further explanation derives the name from the āya marking the break between its surrounding speech.
ITQAN:v1p180/r4.anchor: وقيل لأنها علامة على علامة إنقطاع ما قبلها من الكلام وانقطاعه مما بعدها

ITQAN:v1p180/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p180/r5.speaker: الواحدي
ITQAN:v1p180/r5.claim: Al-Wahidi and some colleagues say that definition could label less than a full āya an āya, except that revelation fixed the divisions as they now stand.
ITQAN:v1p180/r5.anchor: قال الواحدي وبعض أصحابنا يجوز على هذا القول تسمية أقل من الآية آية

ITQAN:v1p180/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p180/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
ITQAN:v1p180/r6.claim: Abu ʿAmr al-Dani says the only word that forms an āya by itself is “mudhāmmatān.”
ITQAN:v1p180/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو الداني لا أعلم كلمة هي وحدها آية إلا قوله ﴿ مدهامتان ﴾

ITQAN:v1p180/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p180/r7.speaker: غيره
ITQAN:v1p180/r7.claim: Other scholars add “wa-l-najm,” “wa-l-duha,” and “wa-l-ʿasr” as standalone āyāt, along with sūra openings for those who count them so.
ITQAN:v1p180/r7.anchor: وقال غيره بل فيه غيرها مثل ﴿ والنجم ﴾ ﴿ والضحى ﴾ ﴿ والعصر ﴾

ITQAN:v1p180/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p180/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v1p180/r8.claim: Some say the correct basis for āya boundaries is prophetic specification: each unit's separation from neighboring speech is known by transmitted instruction, not analogy.
ITQAN:v1p180/r8.anchor: قال بعضهم الصحيح أن الآية إنما تعلم بتوقيف من الشارع كمعرفة السورة

ITQAN:v1p180/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p180/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v1p180/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari likewise says verse counts are transmitted and cannot be inferred by analogy, explaining why some disjointed-letter openings count as āyāt and others do not.
ITQAN:v1p180/r9.anchor: وقال الزمخشري الآيات علم توقيفي لا مجال للقياس فيه ولذلك عدوا ﴿ الم ﴾ آية

ITQAN:v1p180/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p180/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v1p180/r10.claim: Al-Suyuti cites Ahmad's report from Ibn Masʿud that the Prophet recited one of the Hā-Mīm sūras, identified as al-Ahqaf, and used the report's “thirty” designation as evidence about verse counting.
ITQAN:v1p180/r10.anchor: عن زر عن ابن مسعود قال أقرأني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سورة من الثلاثين من آل حم

ITQAN:v1p183/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p183/r1.speaker: الموصلي
ITQAN:v1p183/r1.claim: Al-Mawsili divides sūras into three groups: counts with no disagreement, counts differing in detail only, and counts differing both in total and detail; his lists include forty, four, and seventy sūras respectively.
ITQAN:v1p183/r1.anchor: قال الموصلي ثم سور القرآن على ثلاثة أقسام قسم لم يختلف فيه لا في إجمال ولا في تفصيل

ITQAN:v1p183/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p183/r2.speaker: المدني الأخير والباقون
ITQAN:v1p183/r2.claim: Al-ʿAsr has three verses: the later Medinan count treats “wa-tawāṣaw bi-l-ḥaqq” as a verse but not “wa-l-ʿaṣr”; the other counters do the reverse.
ITQAN:v1p183/r2.anchor: العصر ثلاث عد المدني الأخير ﴿ وتواصوا بالحق ﴾ دون ﴿ والعصر ﴾ وعكس الباقون

ITQAN:v4p432/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p432/r1.speaker: ابن خالويه
ITQAN:v4p432/r1.claim: Al-Suyuti cites Ibn Khalawayh for the letter-count observation that no three-verse sura has ten wāws except al-ʿAṣr through its end.
ITQAN:v4p432/r1.anchor: ولا سورة ثلاث آيات فيها عشر واوات إلا والعصر إلى آخرها

DAMGHANI:v1p325/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p325/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p325/r3.claim: Al-ʿaṣr means time or the passage of time.
DAMGHANI:v1p325/r3.anchor: العصر الدهر قوله سبحانه في سورة العصر
